Definition: a strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses; to crack open (from a fall):--burst asunder.
BiblicalUsage: láschō means to burst asunder — a small word with a sharp edge. In Acts 1:18, "he burst asunder in the midst".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the burst body of the betrayer is Scripture's blunt verdict on treachery — sin does not end neatly, and Judas's end warns me more than any sermon: the price of betraying Christ is paid in full.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
